title: Per-model precision signatures & calibration guidelines (FP8/INT8)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a deterministic, auditable per-model 'precision signature' (recommended FP8/INT8 profiles, acceptable fallbacks, and guardrails) and the calibration + validation workflow required to promote a signature into the model catalog as a default. This ticket codifies heuristics, acceptance thresholds, test harnesses, and rollout steps so product teams can safely use lower-precision defaults without unexpected quality regressions.
background: We have many models in the catalog with ad-hoc quantization notes. Engineering and Product need a single source of truth for per-model precision defaults so downstream routing, Dedicated, and Private deployments can safely apply INT8/FP8 variants. Prior work (safety matrices, calibration harnesses) provides building blocks but lacks a signing and rollout pattern.
proposed_solution: Create a precision-signature artifact for each catalog model: (1) recommendation tag (FP8/INT8/FP16), (2) expected tokenwise throughput uplift, (3) validated accuracy delta bands per workload class, (4) compatible fallback chains, (5) calibration dataset snapshot ids. Implement a CI job that runs the calibration harness, produces signatures, attaches telemetry checks, and stores the signature as an immutable catalog record. Add a human review step for P0/P1 models and an automated gate for lower-risk models.
calibration_workflow: 1) Select representative datasets (prompt suites + task slices) and quantize candidate model variant via calibrated per-layer scaling. 2) Run deterministic calibration harness in shadow mode: generate outputs for baseline FP32/FP16 and candidate FP8/INT8 variants. 3) Compute per-metric deltas (ROUGE/BLEU/EM/LLR/embedding-sim) and distributional drift signals. 4) If deltas within pre-defined bands, mark as 'candidate-signed'. 5) For candidate-signed models, run extended A/B shadow runs on production traffic samples for 48 hours. 6) On pass, create signed precision artifact and push to catalog with rollout policy.
validation_plan: - Define primary accuracy metrics per model family (e.g., LLM: log-likelihood ratio + top-k token accuracy; retrieval/embedding models: cosine shift + downstream ranking). - Minimum pass criteria: median delta <= 1% relative for high-sensitivity models, <=3% for general purpose; p95 accuracy loss <= 5%. - Use stratified evaluation by prompt length, temperature, and instruction complexity. - Automate statistical tests (paired t-test/bootstrapping) and require non-significant regressions at alpha=0.01 for promoted signatures.
telemetry: Collect: token-level latency, tokens/sec, per-request cost estimate delta, model output embedding drift (cosine), task-specific metric deltas, and error/failure rates. Emit signature-level counters and histograms to Console: signature_applied_count, signature_rejected_count, avg_accuracy_delta_{metric}, p95_latency_change. Add alerts for accuracy drift > threshold or error increase > 2x.
rollout_plan: - Stage 1: Shadow-only validation for 48h. - Stage 2: Canary apply to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback on accuracy alert. - Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 50% over 7 days with monitoring. - Stage 4: Full default promotion in catalog and mark as 'recommended'. Provide an explicit rollback path to previous signature or FP16 baseline.
acceptance_criteria: - CI produces a precision-signature artifact and stores it in the catalog for a sample model. - Validation harness demonstrates accuracy deltas within defined bands on at least two representative datasets. - Telemetry hooks and alerts are wired and test alerts trigger on synthetic regressions. - Documentation and runbook exist for reviewers and SRE on rollback.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle distributional failures on long-tail prompts. Mitigation: require extended shadow runs on production-sampled traffic and conservative thresholds for high-sensitivity models. Risk: calibration non-determinism across hardware. Mitigation: pin kernel versions during calibration, capture environment fingerprint in signature, and require parity checks.
open_questions: What minimum benchmark suites must be included per model family?
Who signs off on P1 model signature promotions (Engineering + Product + Ops)?
Should we allow customer-specific precision overrides stored in Private deployments?
